fix_priority.suggested_fix: Lower the Phase 2->Phase 3 gate coverage threshold from 80% to a value achievable with the token-budget-constrained representative-file approach. For codebases with > 200 files, the current formula (max 50k tokens/module) naturally yields ~15-30% file-block coverage. Either: (a) redefine 'coverage' as 'modules with DETAIL.md' / 'total modules' (currently 100%), or (b) set a tiered threshold: >= 80% for < 100-file codebases, >= 40% for 100-300 file codebases, >= 20% for > 300 file codebases.
fix_priority.expected_impact: Fixes S5 FAIL. Removes the false gate criterion that would cause Phase 2 to incorrectly block Phase 3 on large codebases. Also aligns S6 more cleanly as PASS.

summary: 29/30 PASS. The single failure is S5: source_file_coverage_percent = 17.3%, far below the Skill-mandated 80% threshold. This is primarily a Skill calibration defect — the 80% file-block coverage requirement is architecturally incompatible with the token-budget-constrained representative-file DETAIL approach used in Phase 3. With 392 source files and per-module token budgets capping documentation, achieving 80% (314 files with explicit file blocks) would require either dramatically higher budgets or shorter per-file documentation. All other requirements pass: MCP correctly separates structural data from semantic descriptions, all 4 phases executed correctly, all 24 DETAIL files follow the correct format with substantive content, INDEX.md is properly assembled with functional module names and a dependency graph, and the Skill documentation was sufficient to guide correct Agent behavior in all other respects.
